predictions.quote: where this is going to be next year is there's going to be a conductor. And now you will coordinate those five people.
predictions.prediction: By sometime in 2025, commercially available AI systems will include an orchestration/‘conductor’ agent that can coordinate multiple specialized AI agents in roles such as lawyer, accountant, developer, designer, etc., for a user acting as a CEO/founder or product manager.

predictions.quote: In this phase, the the opex of companies will probably be cut in half at the limit.
predictions.prediction: During the current AI-agent adoption cycle (over the next several years), typical operating expenses (opex) for companies will be reducible by roughly 50% as a result of AI agents and automation.

predictions.quote: I think you find that there will be millions and millions and millions and maybe billions of companies. And I think that that's really exciting.
predictions.prediction: Over the long term as AI agents and conductors mature (on a decadal timescale), the number of distinct operating companies globally will grow to at least many millions and potentially into the billions, driven by one-person or very small-team AI-leveraged businesses.

predictions.quote: I definitely think that's kind of what we're seeing.
predictions.prediction: Over the coming years of the AI era, for each major professional services vertical (e.g., lawyers, accountants, artists), market share will concentrate so that one leading vertical AI provider captures the bulk of usage, effectively becoming the default ‘one lawyer service’, ‘one accounting service’, etc., that most users rely on in that vertical.

predictions.quote: 100 million people are soon going to be asking when TikTok gets shut down. 100 million people who used it every day are going to be like, why did this happen?

predictions.quote: What will likely end up happening here is this will find its path to federal preemption. Historically, when we've seen states try to impose these sorts of bans, the companies that are ultimately affected, the innovators that are affected go to the federal government, and they try and legislate for a bill that says this stuff is legal and should be broadly available, that federal preemption then stops states rights on having a ban in place. And so it's very likely that we'll end up seeing some legislation here over the next couple of years if this technology is ultimately beneficial.
predictions.prediction: Within the next couple of years, the U.S. federal government will pass legislation that explicitly legalizes and broadly permits cultivated (lab-grown) meat, preempting state-level bans like Florida’s, provided the technology proves beneficial.

predictions.quote: The problem is, now that Florida has done this, I guarantee you're going to see Texas, which is a huge ranching state, and many other states step up to do it.
predictions.prediction: Following Florida’s ban on cultivated (lab-grown) meat, Texas and multiple other U.S. states will enact similar bans on the manufacture, sale, or distribution of cultivated meat.
